answer: Answer: dentate gyrus. Bad responders show the highest number of significantly differentially expressed genes compared to controls in the dentate gyrus — 245 DEGs under the primary criterion (padj < 0.05, baseMean > 10, |log2FoldChange| > 0.5), versus 93 in baseline blood and 20 in final blood. The ranking (dentate_gyrus > baseline_blood > final_blood) holds under every sensitivity variant tested: one-sided up-only (194 / 88 / 14), the workbook's own DEG-Median or DEG-Max flags intersected with the thresholds (182 / 57 / 18 and 182 / 86 / 19), and the DEG flags alone (202 or 218 / 67 or 207 / 19 or 25). The analysis reuses the authors' precomputed DESeq2 results embedded in the workbook (raw counts are not supplied); the bad-vs-control blocks (2, 5, 8) and their direction (baseMeanA = bad_responder, baseMeanB = Control) were verified programmatically via group-mean matching, not assumed.
